title: What Off-Plan Renderings Don't Show You About Your Unit
seoTitle: What Off-Plan Renderings Don't Show You
description: Off-plan renderings usually show the best unit in the building. Here is how to fill the information gaps and understand the unit you are actually buying.
answer: Most off-plan renderings show the penthouse or the best unit, not yours. To understand what you are buying, collect every piece of information you can (floorplans, price lists, finishes, views, the model) and fill the gaps yourself before you sign.
body:
When you buy off-plan, the developer is supposed to give you enough information to choose the right unit for you: the right layout, the right floor, the right orientation, the right price. In practice, what you receive is a carefully built story.

## What you usually get

- **Renderings**, most often of the penthouse or the best units in the building.
- **Floorplans** for each layout.
- **A price list** and a list of finishes.
- **A sales gallery** with a model of the building and a mock-up kitchen.
- **Brokers**, who guide you through all of it.

All of this is useful. None of it, on its own, shows you your unit.

## The gap between the rendering and your unit

Think about it this way. The images you see are of the best unit, with the best view, in the best light. The one-bedroom you are considering on a lower floor may face a different street, get a different light, and feel very different inside. The rendering sells the building. You are buying one unit inside it.

## Become an investigator

The developer and the brokers control the narrative, and that is their job. Yours is to be the investigator:

- Ask for the floorplan of your exact unit, not the typical layout.
- Ask which way your windows face and what is across the street.
- Compare your unit's price with similar units on other floors.
- Put every piece together until you can picture waking up in that specific space.

## Stay vigilant

Every piece of information you receive was chosen to make the project look its best. That does not make it false. It makes it incomplete, and the gaps are where buyers get surprised. The more of them you fill before signing, the better your decision will be.
takeaways: Renderings usually show the best unit, not the one you are buying.
Developers and brokers control the narrative; you control the questions.
Ask for your exact unit's layout, orientation and view.
Fill every information gap before you sign the contract.
faq: Why don't developers show every unit?
Traditional renderings are expensive, so most developers produce images of a few hero units and the amenities, and leave buyers to imagine the rest.
What should I ask for besides renderings?
The floorplan of your exact unit, its orientation, the floor height, the list of finishes, and anything that shows the real view from your windows.
Is the sales gallery model enough?
A model gives you the shape of the building and its context, but it rarely tells you how your own unit will feel inside or what you will see from it.
